description: Targeted scenarios of the test-mcp-zotero skill (step 3): a row is selected when a changed file matches one of its patterns (exact path, or a directory prefix ending in /**). Read by test/live/agent/prepare.mjs (context.targeted, copy in agent-out/scenarios.json) and by test/live/verify-claims.mjs (claims schema 3: every selected row must be reported).

rows.scenario: search_library without query, each sort with limit: 3, direction asc/desc; an empty query result is a message, not an error
get_collections with include_trashed; get_collection_items on the subcollection (empty: a message) and with excludeAttachments: false (the linked attachment appears)

create_collection with a unicode name (<prefix> Ünïcødé 学习 ✓) under the subcollection (parent_collection = the F2 subcollection) and with a name of only spaces (a readable error, nothing created); claim the new collection with expect.parent_collection

include_abstract: true; an unknown key mixed with known keys: the key → metadata map plus a not_found array, without isError; only unknown keys: an empty result ("No items found for the given keys"), without isError
max_characters: 10 on an item with text; the attachment key directly; unknown key ZZZZZZZZ: isError "Item not found"
add_items with a bookSection (editor), a thesis (university, thesisType) and a conferencePaper; one field invalid for its type must be rejected with a readable message

add_items one journalArticle (run prefix + tag) to edit, get_items_details to read its version, then update_item with that version changing title and pages: re-read shows the new values and a higher version; update_item again with the stale version: isError with code version_conflict and nothing changed; update_item with itemType in fields: rejected before any write; create_note on the same item with two plain-text paragraphs separated by a blank line: it is created as a child. Only ever edit or annotate items this run created

add_items_by_doi with 10.1016/j.cor.2009.01.015 and the nonexistent 10.0000/<prefix> in one call: partial success; claim the item with expect.publicationTitle "Computers & Operations Research" (a literal &, never &); then one DOI in https://doi.org/… form
import_pdf_to_zotero of https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285&type=printable as a child of the article; then get_item_fulltext returns text
find_and_attach_pdfs on the run collection with dry_run: true: processed equals the regular items in it
a standalone linked attachment in both run collections

add_items one book <prefix> T-delete to delete, then delete_items with its key + ZZZZZZZZ: deleted_count 1 and ZZZZZZZZ in not_found; if unsafe_operations is all and not safe mode: create_collection <prefix> T-delete to delete and delete_collection on it. Claim both under deleted
ieee on the author-date document (no num): both producers warn about the missing num and write [?]; claim them with compare_group "nonum-ieee"

a .odt (LibreOffice) document in apa: make-docx --odt an .odt source with <zcite>, then both producers on it — inject_citations (format from the .odt extension) and inject.js via inject.mjs — so content.xml gets reference marks instead of Word fields, the bibliography a text:section, and meta.xml the preferences with fieldType ReferenceMark; claim both with compare_group "odt-apa" (tool vs script, same odt source), which verify-claims fingerprints with its odt branch

create_cited_document from a small Markdown with a heading, bold/italic, a one-level list and pandoc citations ([@K], [@K1; @K2], [see @K, p. 12]) in apa; then the same in ieee (numbers in order of first citation) and as .odt; it never overwrites an existing output; claim the documents
inject.js with the bare numeric user id instead of users/<id> on the apa document: same URIs; claim it, and the inject_citations apa document a second time, with compare_group "bare-id"

prompts/list returns cite_word_document, write_cited_document, import_references and note_from_item with their arguments; prompts/get on note_from_item with the run's article key renders a message that names get_items_details and create_note and contains the key (no leftover ${arguments.…})
per-call library_type: "user" + own library_id on two read tools; get_user_id answers the same library_path; if group_id: repeat the F7 reads

read tools only (never a write tool): get_items_details with item_keys ["ABCD0123"] (0 and 1), ["ABCDEFGO"] (O), ["abcd2345"] (lowercase), ["ABCD234"] (7 characters) and ["../items"]; get_item_fulltext with item_key "../items"; get_collection_items with collection_key "abcd2345": each a validation error with the message "Invalid Zotero key: expected 8 characters from 23456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ" and nothing returned

get_item_fulltext on ZZZZZZZZ, get_collection_items on ZZZZZZZZ and add_items into collection_key ZZZZZZZZ (one book with the run prefix and tag): each an isError with a hint that names the next step (search_library, get_collections), no stack trace
run F1 and T-import (if not already run); every call must return (a success or a clear error)
